description: Attack-decay-sustain-release envelope with exponential stages, built-in velocity scaling, a CV for the sustain level, and a per-voice random spread that makes each channel behave slightly differently

params.text: Sets the rise time, 0.5ms at fully counter-clockwise to 20 seconds at fully clockwise
Sets the fall time from the peak down to the sustain level, 0.5ms to 20 seconds
Sets the level the envelope holds at while the gate is high, 0 to 1
Sets the fall time from wherever the envelope has reached down to zero, 0.5ms to 20 seconds
Sets how much the velocity input scales the envelope's peak, 0 to 1; at 0 the velocity jack does nothing
Scales the attack, decay, sustain and release of each channel by a random amount, 0 to 1, in the way the voices of an old analogue polysynth differ from each other
Attenuates and inverts the Sus jack, -1 to 1, before that voltage is added to the sustain level

inputs.text: The note velocity, 0V to 10V, which scales the envelope's peak by as much as the Vel knob allows
Divided by 10, scaled by the Sus mod knob and added to the sustain level
The gate: the envelope attacks while this is at 1V or above and releases below that; its channel count sets the polyphony of the whole module
A rise past 1V restarts the attack without the gate having to fall first

outputs.text: 10V while the envelope is in its decay or sustain stage, and 0V during the attack and the release; useful for firing a second envelope to shape the sustain

notes: the random spread is generated once per module and saved with the patch, so a patch sounds the same each time it is opened
the polyphony of both outputs follows the gate input alone; the other three jacks are read at whatever channel count that sets

inputs.0:
0 to 10V · continuous · polyphonic

unpatched it reads 0V; a negative voltage does nothing here.
